FXUS62 KMFL 171048
AFDMFL

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Miami FL
548 AM EST Tue Nov 17 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...
Updated at 547 AM EST Tue Nov 17 2026

  - There is an increased threat of urban flooding along the east
    coast of South Florida this week. If repeated rounds of heavy
    rainfall occur, impactful flash flooding is possible. 

  - Flood Watch in effect for all of Southeast Florida through 
    Thursday evening.

  - Dangerous marine conditions are developing across local 
    waters with sustained winds between 20-30 kts with isolated 
    gusts to 35 kts. Atlantic seas are expected to climb to 10-12 
    feet today, with 4-6 feet across Gulf waters.
 
  - Life threatening rip currents and dangerous surf are forecast
    for Miami-Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach beaches through the
    remainder of this week.

&&

.SHORT TERM...
(Today through Wednesday)
Issued at 249 AM EST Tue Nov 17 2026

At the surface, high pressure continues to dominate across the 
eastern seaboard. A weak area of low pressure in the Gulf remains 
the dominant synoptic feature in Florida's unsettled weather pattern 
over the coming days with a mid/upper level shortwave pushing across 
the Gulf coast states through the week. A stationary boundary 
associated with the surface low will remain draped across central 
Florida today, which will begin to pool moisture across the 
peninsula. PWAT values rise into the 1.6-1.7" range which is between 
the 80th-90th percentile for this point in November. As the area of 
low pressure lingers across Gulf waters through the next few days, a 
tight surface pressure gradient will lead to breezy east-northeast 
winds across the region today and tomorrow - especially near the 
immediate east coast where gusts up to 30 mph will be possible. With 
this setup, we're looking at a multi-hazard event through the week 
with 1) an increased threat of urban flooding across the east coast 
2) dangerous marine conditions for small craft and 3) life-
threatening rip currents and high surf at east coast beaches. 

Breezy onshore winds at the surface with strong westerly winds aloft 
create enhanced coastal convergence, where areas along the immediate 
east coast may receive repeated rounds of relentless heavy rainfall 
as ascent is maximized due to low level convergence. At this time, 
the region remains under a Slight (level 2 of 4) risk of Excessive 
Rainfall from the Weather prediction center today and tomorrow. If 
repeated rounds of heavy rainfall occur, impactful urban flash 
flooding will be possible. At this time, most likely widespread 
rainfall totals of 2-4" through Friday are possible along the east 
coast, with a reasonable worst case forecast of 6-10" (10% chance of 
higher totals than these). The Flood Watch has been expanded across 
interior Palm Beach County and Broward and Miami-Dade this morning. 
Although impactful flash flooding will be possible anywhere along 
the east coast, the highest totals are currently forecast across 
coastal Palm Beach and Broward counties as they are closer to the 
stationary boundary. There is always inherent uncertainty in 
these events on where the highest rainfall totals will fall as 
coastal convergence is a complicated process occurring on smaller 
scales that models don't always effectively resolve. 

Not much change in the synoptic setup for Wednesday as the surface 
low will continue to linger in the Gulf, leaving its stationary 
boundary draped across central Florida. PWATs will continue to 
increase through Wednesday with some models showing maximum values 
between 1.8 and even 1.9" by Wednesday night. This is well above the 
90th percentile for this time of year.  

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Wednesday night through Monday)
Issued at 249 AM EST Tue Nov 17 2026

The aforementioned heavy rainfall pattern remains in place Wednesday 
night as a surface low continues to meander across the Gulf leaving 
its attendant stationary boundary draped across the Florida 
peninsula. Model guidance continues to struggle with the exact 
evolution of this feature, and latest runs depict the low remaining 
in the Gulf through the end of the week potentially even into the 
early weekend. High pressure remains entrenched across the eastern 
seaboard at the surface, and finally begins to break down late week 
into early this upcoming weekend as a front pushes across the 
central United States. This could help lift the Gulf low towards the 
northeast, although at this time uncertainty remains high regarding 
the evolution and timing of this motion. PWAT values remain elevated 
(1.7-2.0") on Thursday and Friday, which could lead to a 
continuation of heavy rainfall concerns through even the end of this 
week.  At this time there is a Marginal Risk of excessive rainfall 
along the east coast for Thursday and Friday. The risk is heavily 
dependent on the exact placement of the low and attendant stationary 
boundary, so it isn't totally out of the question that the Flash 
Flooding risk increases for the late week time period in subsequent 
updates. 

As we head into the weekend, most model guidance depicts the Gulf 
low entering the western Atlantic as high pressure breaks down and a 
cold front sweeps across the central United States. This will allow 
it to propagate towards the NE and usher in a much drier air mass 
from the north. PWATs drop between 1-1.3" by the end of the weekend 
into early next week which should act to limit widespread shower and 
storm potential. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 547 AM EST Tue Nov 17 2026

Breezy easterly winds today 15-20 kts with gusts around 30 kts.
Scattered showers and thunderstorms throughout the day which may
result in brief flight restrictions. Outside of convection, SCT to
BKN MVFR ceilings expected.

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 249 AM EST Tue Nov 17 2026

Strengthening northeasterly winds will result in hazardous 
conditions across all local waters of South Florida through the
next couple of days. Strong easterly winds between 25-30 kts will
be likely through the day with isolated gusts to 35 kts possible.
Wave heights are rapidly increasing through the early morning 
hours today with 10-12 foot seas possible by the afternoon hours.
The combination of northeasterly swell during the middle of the 
week may result in even higher wave heights across the Gulfstream 
waters with wave heights potentially reaching 12-14+ feet at 
times. Small Craft Advisories are in effect through Thursday 
night.

&&

.BEACHES...
Issued at 249 AM EST Tue Nov 17 2026

Gusty onshore winds are forecast to increase in strength today, 
resulting in a high risk of life-threatening rip currents at 
Miami- Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach beaches for much of this 
week. A High Surf Advisory is in effect for Palm Beach County 
beaches and Broward County beaches as surf height could reach 7-10
feet through Thursday. 

&&

data.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 17 at 8:09AM EST until November 19 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
data.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Miami Dade County.

* WHEN...Through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
data.instruction:
Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

data.headline: Flood Watch issued November 17 at 8:07AM EST until November 19 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
data.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following
areas, Coastal Broward County, Coastal Miami Dade County, Coastal
Palm Beach County, Far South Miami-Dade County, Inland Broward
County, Inland Miami-Dade County, Inland Palm Beach County, Metro
Broward County, Metro Palm Beach County and Metropolitan Miami
Dade.

* WHEN...From 1 PM EST this afternoon through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Several rounds of storms may produce rainfall amounts of 2 to 4
inches through late Thursday. Higher amounts of 6 to 8 inches
with locally isolated amounts over 10 inches may be possible.
Heavy rainfall rates of 1 to 2 inches per hour may observed with
some of these storms.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
data.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

data.headline: Special Marine Warning issued November 17 at 12:29PM EST until November 17 at 1:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
data.description:
SMWMFL

The National Weather Service in Miami has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL out 20 NM...
Coastal waters from Jupiter Inlet to Deerfield Beach FL out 20
NM...

* Until 100 PM EST.

* At 1229 PM EST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located near Hillsboro Beach, or near Lighthouse
Point, moving west at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Lauderdale-By-The-Sea, Lighthouse Point, Boca Raton, Sea Ranch
Lakes, Hillsboro Beach, Highland Beach, Pompano Beach, Deerfield
Beach, and Fort Lauderdale.
data.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or the National Weather
Service. You can also share your report with NWS Miami on Facebook
and Twitter.
